title: Volume of Cylinders, Cones and Spheres
seo_title: Year 9 Volume Worksheets: Cylinders, Cones, Spheres and Hemispheres (in terms of π)
standard_text: Calculate and solve problems involving: perimeters of 2-D shapes (including circles), areas of circles and composite shapes; surface area and volume of cuboids and other right prisms (including cylinders).
meta_desc: Free Year 9 volume worksheets: volume of cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres, answers to 1 decimal place and in terms of π, capacity and composite solids. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cylinder πr²h, cone ⅓πr²h, sphere ⁴⁄₃πr³.
key_sub: Always use the radius. Halve the diameter first.
body_html:
How it works

Cylinder: V = πr²h (area of the circle × height). Cone: V = ⅓πr²h, one third of the cylinder with the same base and height. Sphere: V = ⁴⁄₃πr³. A hemisphere is half a sphere: ⅔πr³.

Always use the radius. If you are given the diameter, halve it first. An answer “in terms of π” keeps π as a letter, for example 45π cm³.

Example

Cylinder: r = 4 cm, h = 10 cm.

π × 4² × 10 = 160π.

Answer: 502.7 cm³

Example

Cone: r = 3 cm, h = 8 cm.

⅓ × π × 9 × 8 = 24π.

Answer: 75.4 cm³

Example

Sphere: diameter 12 cm.

r = 6 cm.

⁴⁄₃ × π × 216 = 288π.

Answer: 904.8 cm³

Common mistakes

  • Using the diameter instead of the radius.
  • Forgetting the ⅓ in the cone formula.
  • Using 4πr² (surface area) for the volume of a sphere.
  • Mixing units, such as metres and centimetres, in one calculation.

faq.q: What is the formula for the volume of a cylinder?
faq.a: V = πr²h: the area of the circular end multiplied by the height.

faq.q: Why is a cone one third of a cylinder?
faq.a: A cone with the same base and height as a cylinder holds exactly one third as much, so V = ⅓πr²h.

faq.q: What is the volume of a sphere?
faq.a: V = ⁴⁄₃πr³. For a hemisphere, halve it: ⅔πr³.

faq.q: What does 'in terms of π' mean?
faq.a: Leave π as a symbol instead of using 3.14…. For example a cylinder with r = 3 and h = 5 has volume 45π cm³.

items.q: An ice cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, with a hemisphere of ice cream on top of radius 3 cm. Find the total volume in terms of π.
items.e: Cone: ⅓ × π × 9 × 10 = 30π. Hemisphere: ⅔ × π × 27 = 18π. Total: 48π cm³.

items.q: A ball has diameter 22 cm. What is its volume to the nearest cm³?
If the radius of a sphere doubles, what happens to its volume?
items.e: Volume depends on r³, and 2³ = 8, so it is multiplied by 8.

items.q: If the height of a cylinder doubles and the radius stays the same, what happens to its volume?
items.e: V = πr²h and only h doubles, so it doubles.

items.q: If the radius of a cylinder doubles and the height stays the same, what happens to its volume?
items.e: V depends on r², and 2² = 4, so it is multiplied by 4.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of a cone?
items.e: A cone is one third of a cylinder: ⅓πr²h.

items.q: Which formula gives the volume of a sphere?
A pipe is a cylinder 2 m long with radius 3 cm. What is its volume in cm³, to the nearest whole number?
A cylindrical glass of radius 4 cm is filled with 400 cm³ of water. How deep is the water, to 1 decimal place?
Which holds more: a cylinder with radius 3 cm and height 4 cm, or a sphere with radius 3 cm?
items.e: Cylinder: π × 9 × 4 = 36π cm³. Sphere: ⁴⁄₃ × π × 27 = 36π cm³. They hold the same.

items.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and made into a cylinder of radius 6 cm. How tall is the cylinder?
items.e: Sphere: ⁴⁄₃π × 216 = 288π. Cylinder: π × 36 × h = 288π, so h = 8 cm.

items.e: The radius is 5 cm, not 10 cm: π × 5² × 4 = 100π cm³. Leo got 400π.
